And honestly, guaranteed money is more important than the per year money anyway. Sure you can sign a 4 year $100m contract, but if the last year is a $30m non-guaranteed salary, you can bet that that contract is a 4 year $70m deal with the player either being cut of forced to renegotiate. Hell, just look at Joe Flacco's contract, it's essentially a 3 year deal with how the cap numbers go up for the last 3 years.

I think the big picture here is people forget how much the cap expands, and how Megatron money was only relevant to the percentage of the cap when it was signed. I think the cap has went up 25mil since then? I'm not arguing Dez should get Megatron money, but that should be a starting point for negotiation. Dez is a top receiver and with the cap going up, he would be paid like it on the open market.
